To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the imidazolim-based ionic liquid [BMIM][BF(4)] alters the self-assembled structures of the lipid monolayer and bilayer and reduces the in-plane elasticity of these layers.

the IL alters the pressure- area isotherm of monolayer formed from DPPC lipid at an air- water interface and the in-plane elasticity of DPPC monolayer is reduced due to the insertion of this ionic liquid.

the interaction of an ionic liquid with a soft lipid bilayer is dependent on the chain configuration of the lipid and that the IL perturbs the lipid membrane by decreasing the in-plane elastic modulus of the lipid monolayer and increasing the thickness of the lipid bilayer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of an IL with a lipid membrane and the effect of the interaction on the membrane structure.
the interaction of an IL with a model lipid membrane and its effects on the structural properties of the bilayer.
the interaction of a biologically important ionic liquid with a soft supported lipid bilayer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IL interacts strongly with the soft supported lipid bilayer, but its interaction with the lipid monolayer is not as strong.
the ILs can interact with the lipid bilayer and alter the self-assembled bilayer structure.
the IL interacts with the membrane and perturbs its structure, which is the basis for the antimicrobial activity of the ILs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ILs can be used as an antimicrobial agent and the mechanism is likely to be the perturbation of the lipid layer.
the ILs interact with the lipid bilayers in such a way that the lipid chains become more compact, and the polar head groups are more exposed, which may result in the leakage of the membrane.
the ILs are found to have a strong effect on the structure of the lipid membranes and that this effect depends on the chain configurations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ILs interact with the cell membrane, which is a soft lipid bilayer, by inserting into it and thereby perturb its structure.
the interaction of the IL with the cell membranes leads to perturbations in the lipid bilayer structure, which may be the reason for the antimicrobial activity of ILs.
the IL is found to be a potent antibacterial agent and can be used to alter the properties of the lipid bilayer.
